tunings.label: Drop D
tunings.notes: D A D G B E
tunings.prompt: guitars in drop D tuning, heavy one-finger power chords chugging on the low D string
tunings.desc: Only the low E drops a whole step to D, for one-finger power chords and a deeper low end. Grunge, alt-rock, metal and folk.

tunings.label: Drop C
tunings.notes: C G C F A D
tunings.prompt: guitars in drop C tuning, crushing low C power chords and dark, heavy riffs
tunings.desc: D standard with the low string dropped another whole step to C. The core sound of metalcore, nu-metal and post-hardcore.

tunings.label: D standard
tunings.notes: D G C F A D
tunings.prompt: guitars in D standard tuning, a whole step down for a darker, looser, heavier tone
tunings.desc: Every string a whole step below standard. Thick, slack tone for grunge, doom, stoner rock and heavy blues, and friendlier for lower voices.

tunings.label: Eb standard
tunings.notes: Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb
tunings.prompt: guitars tuned a half step down to Eb, warm, slightly slack tone with easy string bends
tunings.desc: Every string a half step below standard. A classic for blues-rock, 80s hard rock, grunge and shred; looser strings make bends easier.

tunings.label: DADGAD
tunings.notes: D A D G A D
tunings.prompt: acoustic guitar in DADGAD tuning, droning open strings and ringing modal, Celtic-flavored chords
tunings.desc: A suspended open tuning, neither major nor minor, that rings with drones. Loved in Celtic, folk, fingerstyle and ambient acoustic music.

tunings.label: Open G
tunings.notes: D G D G B D
tunings.prompt: guitar in open G tuning, ringing open-chord riffs and slide guitar with a loose, swaggering feel
tunings.desc: The open strings form a G major chord. Behind countless slide-blues licks and swaggering classic rock riffs.

tunings.label: Open D
tunings.notes: D A D F# A D
tunings.prompt: guitar in open D tuning, big resonant open chords and bottleneck slide
tunings.desc: The open strings form a D major chord. Rich and resonant for slide blues, folk, fingerstyle and singer-songwriter songs.

tunings.label: Open E
tunings.notes: E B E G# B E
tunings.prompt: guitar in open E tuning, bright, tense ringing chords and fiery electric slide
tunings.desc: The open D shape a whole step higher, so it sounds brighter and tighter. A favorite for electric slide blues and Southern rock.

tunings.label: Baritone B
tunings.notes: B E A D F# B
tunings.prompt: baritone guitar tuned to B, deep twangy low melodies and a dark cinematic tone
tunings.desc: A longer-scale guitar tuned a fourth below standard. Used for surf-noir, spaghetti-western themes, country tic-tac bass lines and modern heavy music.

tunings.label: 7-string B standard
tunings.notes: B E A D G B E
tunings.prompt: seven-string guitars in B standard, the extended low B string driving syncopated djent-style chugs
tunings.desc: Standard tuning plus a low B below the E. The basis of nu-metal, djent and progressive metal, and also used for jazz chord-melody.

tunings.label: 4-string bass standard
tunings.prompt: electric bass in standard E A D G tuning, round and punchy low end
tunings.desc: The standard four-string bass, an octave below the guitar's four lowest strings. Covers almost every style.

tunings.label: 5-string bass low B
tunings.prompt: five-string bass with a low B string, deep sub-heavy notes reaching below standard bass range
tunings.desc: Adds a low B under the E for notes down to about 31 Hz. Standard in gospel, modern R&B, metal and session work.

tunings.label: A=432 Hz
tunings.notes: E A D G B E (reference A4 = 432 Hz)
tunings.prompt: tuned to A=432 Hz, slightly lower and mellower than standard concert pitch
tunings.desc: Moves the reference pitch from A=440 Hz down about 32 cents. Popular in meditation and ambient circles; the warmth it is said to add is a matter of taste.

edits.label: New song (full prompt)
edits.example:
Neo-soul with late-90s production, mellow and warm. Rhodes electric piano, round bass, soft live drums with ghost notes. 84 BPM in Eb major, loose swung groove. Smooth male baritone vocal with falsetto on the hook, sung in English.

Lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Sunday light across the floor
[Chorus]
Stay a little longer
edits.when: Starting a New session and you want a complete song in Google's recommended order.

edits.label: New instrumental
edits.template: {genre}, {mood}. {instruments}. {bpm} BPM in {key}, {groove}. Instrumental, melody carried by {lead}. {production}.
edits.example: Synthwave, nostalgic and driving. Analog polysynth pads, pulsing octave bass, gated reverb snare. 100 BPM in A minor, steady motorik groove. Instrumental, melody carried by a soaring analog synth lead. Wide stereo and warm tape saturation.
edits.when: For beats, beds and scores where the whole track should be vocal-free.

edits.label: Timestamped arrangement
edits.example:
Cinematic ambient, hopeful, 90 BPM in D major, instrumental.
[00:00] soft felt piano intro
[00:30] warm strings enter
[01:00] drums and bass build
[01:45] full orchestral climax
[02:30] piano alone to close
edits.when: When things must happen at exact moments, such as a drop timed to a video cut.

edits.label: 30-second hook
edits.template:
{genre}, {mood}. Short 30-second track that opens cold on the hook. {instruments}. {bpm} BPM in {key}. {vocals}, sung in {language}.

Lyrics:
[Chorus]
{hook}
edits.example:
Upbeat pop, playful and confident. Short 30-second track that opens cold on the hook. Plucked synth, handclaps, deep bass. 120 BPM in G major. Bright female vocal with stacked harmonies, sung in English.

Lyrics:
[Chorus]
Main character, watch me glow
edits.when: For reels, shorts and ads where the first three seconds decide everything.

edits.label: Change the lyrics
edits.template:
Keep the melody and arrangement of the {section}, and change the lyrics to:
{lyrics}
edits.example:
Keep the melody and arrangement of the chorus, and change the lyrics to:
[Chorus]
We were gold in the summer light
Holding on through the longest night
edits.when: The song works but a line or a whole section needs new words.

edits.label: Swap an instrument
edits.template: Replace the {old_instrument} with {instrument}, playing the same part with {detail}.
edits.example: Replace the synth lead with a muted trumpet, playing the same melody with a soft, breathy tone.
edits.when: You like the song but one sound feels wrong for it.

edits.label: Shift the mood
edits.template: Make the whole song more {mood}: {changes}.
edits.example: Make the whole song more melancholy: minor-key chords, slower half-time drums, softer pads and a more fragile vocal.
edits.when: The arrangement is right but the emotion needs to move.

edits.label: Change tempo or key
edits.template: Change the tempo to {bpm} BPM and the key to {key}, keeping the same melody and arrangement.
edits.example: Change the tempo to 92 BPM and the key to D minor, keeping the same melody and arrangement.
edits.when: The groove feels rushed or dragging, or the vocal sits too high or too low.

edits.label: Change the singer
edits.template: Change the lead vocal to {vocal}, singing the same melody and lyrics.
edits.example: Change the lead vocal to a warm male baritone with a light rasp, singing the same melody and lyrics.
edits.when: The voice clashes with the character of the song.

edits.label: Change the mix
edits.template: Give the mix {production}, with {detail}.
edits.example: Give the mix warm tape saturation and vinyl crackle, with a softer top end and a drier, closer vocal.
edits.when: The parts are right and the sound needs a new finish.

edits.label: Add a layer
edits.template: Add {instrument} to the {section}, playing {part}.
edits.example: Add a lush string section to the final chorus, playing long sustained chords that swell into each downbeat.
edits.when: A section feels thin and needs one more element.

edits.label: Extend with an outro
edits.template: Extend the song with a {bars}-bar outro that {ending}.
edits.example: Extend the song with an 8-bar outro that strips back to piano and vocal and fades out on the main melody.
edits.when: The song stops abruptly or you need a proper ending.

edits.label: Add a second verse
edits.template: Continue with a second verse in the same style, {detail}, then return to the chorus.
edits.example: Continue with a second verse in the same style, adding a guitar counter-melody and slightly busier drums, then return to the chorus.
edits.when: The first generation is short and the story needs more room before the hook returns.

edits.label: Long DJ-friendly outro
edits.template: Extend with a {bars}-bar DJ-friendly outro: drums and bass carry the groove while {elements} drop away every 8 bars, ending on {final}.
edits.example: Extend with a 32-bar DJ-friendly outro: drums and bass carry the groove while pads, vocal and percussion drop away every 8 bars, ending on kick and hats alone.
edits.when: For club tracks a DJ needs to mix out of.

edits.label: Add an instrumental break
edits.template: Continue with a {bars}-bar instrumental {instrument} solo over the chorus chords, then a final chorus.
edits.example: Continue with an 8-bar instrumental saxophone solo over the chorus chords, then a final chorus.
edits.when: You want a breather or a showcase moment before the end.

edits.label: Bigger final chorus
edits.template: Continue with a double final chorus that {lift}, then end on {ending}.
edits.example: Continue with a double final chorus that modulates up a half step with gospel ad-libs and a choir, then end on a held final chord.
edits.when: The song needs a bigger payoff at the end.

edits.label: Acoustic version
edits.template: Cover this song as an acoustic version: {instruments}, {mood}, same melody and lyrics, {vocal}.
edits.example: Cover this song as an acoustic version: fingerpicked acoustic guitar, soft cello and light percussion, intimate and warm, same melody and lyrics, close-miked breathy vocal.
edits.when: For an unplugged take with a quieter, live-session feel.

edits.label: Orchestral version
edits.template: Cover this song as a {style} orchestral version: {instruments}, same melody, {tempo}.
edits.example: Cover this song as a cinematic orchestral version: string orchestra, French horns, harp and timpani, same melody carried by the strings, slower and grander at 72 BPM.
edits.when: For trailers, intros or a dramatic reimagining.

edits.label: 80s synth version
edits.template: Cover this song as a 1980s synth-pop version: {instruments}, gated reverb drums, same melody and lyrics, {vocal}.
edits.example: Cover this song as a 1980s synth-pop version: analog polysynths, pulsing octave bass and a LinnDrum-style kit, gated reverb drums, same melody and lyrics, cool reverb-drenched vocal.
edits.when: To give a modern song a retro neon twist.

edits.label: Lo-fi version
edits.template: Cover this song as a lo-fi hip-hop version at {bpm} BPM: {instruments}, swung dusty drums, vinyl crackle, {vocal}.
edits.example: Cover this song as a lo-fi hip-hop version at 78 BPM: Rhodes chords and soft bass, swung dusty drums, vinyl crackle, instrumental with the melody carried by a muted guitar.
edits.when: To turn any song into a chill study or background version.

edits.label: Rock version
edits.template: Cover this song as a {style} rock version: {instruments}, live drums, same melody and lyrics, {vocal}.
edits.example: Cover this song as a punchy pop-rock version: overdriven guitars and driving bass, live drums with crash-heavy choruses, same melody and lyrics, raspy belted vocal.
edits.when: To give a soft song more energy and grit.

edits.label: Restyle as any genre
edits.template: Cover this song as {genre}: {instruments}, {bpm} BPM, {mood}, keeping the melody and lyrics.
edits.example: Cover this song as bossa nova: nylon guitar, brushed drums, upright bass and flute, 128 BPM, breezy and intimate, keeping the melody and lyrics.
edits.when: To hear how the same tune feels in a completely different world.

edits.label: Harder drop
edits.template: Replace the {section} with a harder drop: {detail}.
edits.example: Replace the second drop with a harder drop: distorted growling bass, a heavier half-time kick and snare, and a big impact on the downbeat.
edits.when: The drop lands but lacks punch.

edits.label: New bridge
edits.template: Replace the bridge with {style}: {detail}.
edits.example: Replace the bridge with a stripped-back breakdown: piano and vocal alone on new chords from the relative minor, building back with drums into the last chorus.
edits.when: The bridge repeats the chorus energy and needs real contrast.

edits.label: Cleaner intro
edits.template: Replace the intro with a cleaner {bars}-bar intro: {detail}.
edits.example: Replace the intro with a cleaner 4-bar intro: solo piano stating the chorus melody, then the beat drops in.
edits.when: The intro is muddy, too busy or slow to get going.

edits.label: Shorten the intro
edits.template: Shorten the intro to {bars} bars.
edits.example: Shorten the intro to 4 bars.
edits.when: Listeners need to reach the vocal or hook faster, especially for streaming and short-form.

edits.label: Add a bridge
edits.template: Add a bridge before the final chorus: {detail}.
edits.example: Add a bridge before the final chorus: half-time drums, new chords and a whispered vocal that builds back up.
edits.when: The song runs verse-chorus-verse-chorus and starts to feel repetitive.

edits.label: Bigger chorus
edits.template: Replace the {section} with a bigger version: {detail}.
edits.example: Replace the last chorus with a bigger version: stacked harmonies, a choir, wider stereo synths and a key change up a half step.
edits.when: A chorus feels flat compared with the rest of the song.

edits.label: Vocal stem (a cappella)
edits.template: Split this song into stems in a Space and export the vocals stem as an a cappella for {use}.
edits.example: Split this song into stems in a Space and export the vocals stem as an a cappella for a remix over a house beat.
edits.when: You want to remix the vocal or reuse it over a new beat.

edits.label: Drums stem
edits.template: Split this song into stems in a Space and use the drums stem to {use}.
edits.example: Split this song into stems in a Space and use the drums stem to layer under my own production, or to study the groove hit by hit.
edits.when: You love the groove and want to reuse it or learn from it.

edits.label: Bass stem
edits.template: Split this song into stems in a Space and use the bass stem to {use}.
edits.example: Split this song into stems in a Space and use the bass stem to transcribe the bass line, then replay it on a TR-808-style sub.
edits.when: To learn the bass line, replay it, or rebalance the low end.

edits.label: Instrumental / karaoke
edits.template: Split this song into stems in a Space and mute the vocals stem to make an instrumental for {use}.
edits.example: Split this song into stems in a Space and mute the vocals stem to make an instrumental for karaoke or a video background.
edits.when: You need the backing track on its own.

edits.label: Tighten the hook
edits.template: Rewrite the {section} so the hook is one short {length} line that repeats {times} and lands on the downbeat.
edits.example: Rewrite the chorus so the hook is one short six-word line that repeats twice and lands on the downbeat.
edits.when: The chorus is wordy and hard to sing back.

edits.label: Add internal rhyme
edits.template: Rewrite the {section} with internal rhymes inside each line, keeping the same meaning and syllable count.
edits.example: Rewrite the second verse with internal rhymes inside each line, keeping the same meaning and syllable count.
edits.when: Rap or pop verses feel flat and need more bounce.

edits.label: Switch to second person
edits.template: Rewrite the lyrics in second person, speaking directly to {who} as 'you', keeping the story and rhyme scheme.
edits.example: Rewrite the lyrics in second person, speaking directly to an old friend as 'you', keeping the story and rhyme scheme.
edits.when: The song feels distant and should sound like a direct conversation.

edits.label: Add concrete imagery
edits.template: Rewrite the {section} with concrete images of {setting}, swapping abstract words for things you can see, hear and touch.
edits.example: Rewrite the first verse with concrete images of a rainy bus stop at night, swapping abstract words for things you can see, hear and touch.
edits.when: The lyrics lean on cliches like 'heart' and 'forever'.

edits.label: Translate a section
edits.template: Rewrite the {section} in {language}, keeping the same melody, syllable count and meaning.
edits.example: Rewrite the chorus in Spanish, keeping the same melody, syllable count and meaning.
edits.when: For a bilingual hook or a version for another audience, in any of Flow's vocal languages.
